arxiv-2112-15312.title: Improving heavy Dirac neutrino prospects at future hadron colliders using machine learning
arxiv-2112-15312.creator: Jie Feng, Mingqiu Li, Qi-Shu Yan, Yu-Pan Zeng, Hong-Hao Zhang, Yongchao Zhang, Zhijie Zhao
arxiv-2112-15312.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jie Feng, Mingqiu Li, Qi-Shu Yan, Yu-Pan Zeng, Hong-Hao Zhang, Yongchao Zhang, Zhijie Zhao. In this work, by using the machine learning methods, we study the sensitivities of heavy pseudo-Dirac neutrino N N in the inverse seesaw at the high-energy hadron colliders.

arxiv-2304-00955.title: A short note on the paper ‘Are Randomized Caches Really Random?’ [ 4 ]
arxiv-2304-00955.creator: Anirban Chakraborty, Sarani Bhattacharya, Sayandeep Saha, Debdeep Mukhopadhyay
arxiv-2304-00955.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyse the results and claims presented in the paper ‘Are Randomized Caches Truly Random? Formal Analysis of Randomized Partitioned Caches’ , presented at HPCA conference 2023. In addition, we also analyse the applicability of ‘Bucket and Ball’ analytical model presented in MIRAGE [ 6 ] for its security estimation.

arxiv-2403-03833.title: Superfluid dark stars
arxiv-2403-03833.creator: Lorenzo Cipriani, Massimo Mannarelli, Fabrizio Nesti, Silvia Trabucco
arxiv-2403-03833.description: Abstract We present a superfluid dark star model consisting of relativistic dark bosons with two-body self-interaction. The obtained masses, radii, and tidal deformability depend in a simple way on the boson mass and interaction strength. We report first results on binary mergers: the distinctive amplitude and frequency of the emitted gravitational waves are well within reach of terrestrial interferometers.

arxiv-2410-09127.title: CYCLE: Cross-Year Contrastive Learning in Entity-Linking
arxiv-2410-09127.creator: Pengyu Zhang, Congfeng Cao, Klim Zaporojets, Paul Groth
arxiv-2410-09127.description: Abstract . Knowledge graphs constantly evolve with new entities emerging, existing definitions being revised, and entity relationships changing. These changes lead to temporal degradation in entity linking models, characterized as a decline in model performance over time. To address this issue, we propose leveraging graph relationships to aggregate information from neighboring entities across different time periods.

arxiv-2503-23221.title: Modeling Maximum drawdown Records with Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processe in Capital Markets
arxiv-2503-23221.creator: Rolando Rubilar-Torrealba, Lisandro Fermin, Soledad Torres
arxiv-2503-23221.description: Abstract We propose to model the records of the maximum Drawdown in capital markets by means a Piecewise Deterministic Markov Process (PDMP). We derive statistical results such as the mean and variance that describes the sequence of maximum Drawdown records.

pmc-11420241.title: Glypican-3-targeted macrophages delivering drug-loaded exosomes offer efficient cytotherapy in mouse models of solid tumours
pmc-11420241.creator: Jinhu Liu, Huajun Zhao, Tong Gao, Xinyan Huang, Shujun Liu, Meichen Liu, Weiwei Mu, Shuang Liang, Shunli Fu, Shijun Yuan, Qinglin Yang, Panpan Gu, Nan Li, Qingping Ma, Jie Liu, Xinke Zhang, Na Zhang, Yongjun Liu
pmc-11420241.description: Cytotherapy is a strategy to deliver modified cells to a diseased tissue, but targeting solid tumours remains challenging. Here we design macrophages, harbouring a surface glypican-3-targeting peptide and carrying a cargo to combat solid tumours. The anchored targeting peptide facilitates tumour cell recognition by the engineered macrophages, thus enhancing specific targeting and phagocytosis of tumour cells expressing glypican-3.

pmc-11587106.title: Transcriptomic Evidence for Cell-Autonomous Sex Differentiation of the Gynandromorphic Fat Body in the Silkworm, Bombyx mori
pmc-11587106.creator: Fumiko Yamamoto, Takeshi Yokoyama, Yan Su, Masataka G. Suzuki
pmc-11587106.description: The classic model of sex determination in insects suggests that they do not have sex hormones and that sex is determined in a cell-autonomous manner. On the other hand, there is accumulating evidence that the development of secondary sexual traits is controlled in a non-cell-autonomous manner through external factors.

pmc-12718723.title: The Trendelenburg position decreases the threshold of dynamic variables in predicting fluid responsiveness: A prospective observational study
pmc-12718723.creator: Chih-Chung Wu, Eric Yi-Hsiu Huang, Hui-Hsuan Ke, Yu-Hsien Wang, Wen-Kuei Chang, Chien-Kun Ting
pmc-12718723.description: Background:Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) individualizes fluid administration to optimize oxygen delivery and tissue perfusion. Traditional static parameters, such as central venous and pulmonary artery wedge pressures, are inaccurate. Instead, GDFT employs dynamic variables like stroke volume variation (SVV) and pulse pressure variation (PPV) to assess preload responsiveness and guide fluid administration.

pmc-13332858.title: Reported Effectiveness of a Text‐Based Post‐Operative Care Intervention After Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision (VMMC) to Improve Quality of Care and Adverse Events Identification in Sub‐Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review
pmc-13332858.creator: Calsile Makhele, Evans Duah, Smangaliso Morerwa, Kuhlula Maluleke
pmc-13332858.description: Background and AimAlthough the two‐way texting (2wT) intervention is a promising mobile‐health (mHealth) approach, limited research exists on its implementation, acceptability and potential benefits within Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision (VMMC) context. This scoping review mapped the available literature on 2wT's application in VMMC post‐operative care, focusing on outcomes related to quality of care and adverse event identification in Sub‐Saharan Africa.

pmc-13478888.title: Diversity representation in the development of respiratory society guidance documents
pmc-13478888.creator: Josephine Younan, Tong Hieu, Emma Marshall, Latisha E. Witjaksono, Arwel W. Jones, Seema Green, Yuxin Jiao, William Soon, Kirushallini Saravanan, Pulasthi V. Wettesinghe, Christopher J. Ryerson, Kevin C. Wilson, Yet Hong Khor
pmc-13478888.description: IntroductionSocietal guidance documents, typically developed by diverse and multidisciplinary committees, are pivotal in supporting patient care and advancing research to improve respiratory health. This study evaluated panel member composition of guidance documents developed by two international respiratory societies, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) and the European Respiratory Society (ERS).
